title: EnvironmentDialog: Delete/Rename/Import write to disk instantly — the Cancel button does not cancel anything
existing_state: The dialog presents a standard Save/Cancel pair (EnvironmentDialog.cs:249-250, _btnCancel has DialogResult.Cancel), but every action button mutates persistent state at click time: BtnDelete_Click calls _environmentService.DeleteEnvironment + _presetManager.ClearFolderBaseEnvironment (EnvironmentDialog.cs:496-501), BtnRename_Click calls RenameEnvironment + RenameFolderBaseEnvironment (470-473), BtnImport_Click calls ImportEnvironment with overwriteExisting (595), and every list selection change pushes description/color/variables through UpdateEnvironmentDetails (403-413 -> 802-823). All of these end in ConfigurationService.SaveEnvironmentState which writes config.json immediately (Services/EnvironmentService.cs:207, 323-326). BtnSave_Click's only real effect is setting SelectedEnvironmentName so Form1 switches environments (EnvironmentDialog.cs:639-643; Form1.cs:1941-1944). A user who deletes or renames an environment and then clicks Cancel has still permanently destroyed it — all its variables, description, and vault-profile binding are gone with no undo and no indication that Cancel was ineffective.
recommendation: Make the dialog operate on an in-memory working copy (clone of the environment map) and commit through EnvironmentService only in BtnSave_Click; Cancel then discards the working copy. If a full staging refactor is too invasive, the minimal fix is (a) remove the Cancel button and relabel Save to Close so the UI stops lying, and (b) keep the per-action confirmation prompts. Either way the current Save/Cancel pair must not remain as-is.
user_benefit: Prevents permanent, unrecoverable loss of an environment (and its variables) by a user who reasonably believes Cancel reverts their session.

evidence.note: Destructive ops fire immediately; Save only sets SelectedEnvironmentName; Cancel closes with DialogResult.Cancel and reverts nothing
DeleteEnvironment and UpdateEnvironmentDetails both call SaveEnvironmentState (disk write) synchronously
Form1 only consumes SelectedEnvironmentName on OK; Cancel path returns early
